Seminar Title:

Evolution of the Dalma meta-igneous suite and associated felsic rocks: implications for the tectonic history of the North Singhbhum Mobile Belt, Eastern India

Abstract:

The Dalma meta-igneous suite of the North Singhbhum Mobile Belt (NSMB) represents an important Mesoproterozoic mafic magmatic belt whose tectonic evolution remains incompletely understood. This study integrates field geology, structural analysis, petrography, mineral chemistry, and metamorphic pressure-temperature (P-T) estimates to characterize the lithological, structural, and metamorphic evolution of the suite. Field investigations show that the Dalma meta-igneous suite is composed predominantly of foliated mafic to ultramafic rocks, whereas granitoids and supracrustal rocks occur to the north and south. Three generations of planar fabrics (S1, S2, and S3) are recognized, with S2 representing the dominant regional foliation that is locally refolded and transposed by a later penetrative S3 fabric. Petrographic observations reveal mineral assemblages comprising hornblende, plagioclase, chlorite, epidote-clinozoisite, quartz, titanite, and ilmenite, together with locally preserved hornblende- and plagioclase-rich globular domains interpreted as relict igneous features. Mineral chemistry identifies hornblende and actinolite amphiboles, albite-andesine plagioclase, and clinochlore-ripidolite chlorite. Amphibole-plagioclase thermometry and amphibole barometry yield metamorphic conditions of 450&ndash660 &degC and 6&ndash12 kbar, whereas hornblende-rich globular domains record 580&ndash660 &degC and 5.5&ndash10.8 kbar. These P-T estimates indicate metamorphism under amphibolite-facies conditions. The integrated dataset demonstrates that the Dalma meta-igneous suite preserves evidence of multiple deformation events, regional metamorphism, and localized high-strain zones, providing new constraints on the tectonic evolution of the Dalma belt within the NSMB.
